I hope this letter finds you well. I am writing from your kitchen, where the plates are piled high, the bowls are stained, and the water is running cold.

Your hands were tired last night, and they carry that burden into every room of our house. Your work has not rested on its own; it was shared with me, and we both carried the load. Tonight would be an opportunity for real change. Ask if washing takes too long or if there is no one else who can help. Let us make it happen together.

Take care,
A friend

response: No. People choose their houses because they can pay for them, not because of who gets the land that holds it. Coastal communities bear the brunt of sea-level rise, storm surges and flooding; island nations with no landfalls suffer most from cyclones and droughts; farmers in low-lying areas lose their fields to saltwater intrusion; cities built on high ground struggle hardest. Wealthier countries have often sent more money into adaptation than they have onto vulnerable ones. A just response depends on who gets the funding, the resources and the power to decide what that means for each one of us.
